```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "C:/Users/annae/Downloads/business_intelligence/data/midwest_airbnb_extended.db")
listings     = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
availability = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "availability_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
reviews      = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "reviews_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

## Task 1
```{r}
if(require(dplyr) == FALSE) install.packages("dplyr")

# Count listings per host_id, across ALL cities combined
host_counts <- listings |>
  dplyr::count(host_id, name = "host_listing_count")

#Join the count back onto the full listings table
listings_joined <- listings |>
  dplyr::left_join(host_counts, by = "host_id")

# How many unique hosts have 10+ listings?
a1_big_hosts <- host_counts |>
  dplyr::filter(host_listing_count >= 10)

n_big_hosts <- nrow(a1_big_hosts)
n_big_hosts
# 198
# What percent of Chicago's listings do those big hosts hold?
chicago_listings <- listings_joined |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Chicago")

chicago_total <- nrow(chicago_listings)

chicago_big_host_listings <- chicago_listings |>
  dplyr::filter(host_listing_count >= 10) |>
  nrow()

pct_chicago_big_hosts <- (chicago_big_host_listings / chicago_total) * 100
pct_chicago_big_hosts
# 31.89945, 32%

```

## Task 2
```{r}

family_listings <- listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    accommodates >= 4,
    number_of_reviews >= 10,
    review_scores_rating >= 4.8
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person = price / accommodates)

# Median price per person, grouped by city and neighbourhood
#  count listings per group for 20+ threshold
neighbourhood_summary <- family_listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, neighbourhood) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price_per_person = median(price_per_person, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_listings = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Keep  neighbourhoods with >20 qualifying listings
neighbourhood_summary_filtered <- neighbourhood_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(n_listings >= 20)

# Columbus neighbourhood with the lowest med price per person
a3_result <- neighbourhood_summary_filtered |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |>
  dplyr::arrange(median_price_per_person)

a3_result
# North Linden

```

## Task 3
```{r}
city_room_summary <- listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, room_type) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      c(price, reviews_per_month, estimated_revenue_l365d),
      ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      .names = "median_{.col}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

city_room_summary

a4_result <- city_room_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities", room_type == "Entire home/apt")

a4_result
# $19,619
```

## Task 4
```{r}
concentration_summary <- listings |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(estimated_revenue_l365d)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    rank_in_city = dplyr::row_number(),
    cutoff = ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n()),
    is_top_10_pct = rank_in_city <= cutoff
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_revenue = sum(estimated_revenue_l365d),
    top_10_pct_revenue = sum(estimated_revenue_l365d[is_top_10_pct]),
    pct_revenue_from_top_10_pct = (top_10_pct_revenue / total_revenue) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

concentration_summary

# A5: Columbus's percent of revenue earned by its top 10%
a5_result <- concentration_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus")

a5_result
# 36.1%
```

## Task 5
```{r}


availability_oct <- availability |>
  dplyr::filter(month == "2026-10")


entire_homes <- listings |>
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt")


entire_homes_oct <- entire_homes |>
  dplyr::inner_join(availability_oct, by = "id")


city_share_summary <- entire_homes_oct |>
  dplyr::mutate(mostly_taken = nights_available < 0.5 * nights_in_month) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    share_mostly_taken = mean(mostly_taken, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_listings = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(share_mostly_taken)

city_share_summary

# A6 & A7: city with the LOWEST share, and that share itself
a6_a7_result <- city_share_summary |>
  dplyr::slice(1)

a6_a7_result
# Columbus, and 0.19 or 19%

```

## Task 6
```{r}
if(require(dplyr) == FALSE) install.packages("dplyr")

# Step 1: Join reviews to listings to bring in city
reviews_with_city <- reviews |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    listings |> dplyr::select(id, city),
    by = "id"
  )

# Step 2-3: Filter to July 2025 - June 2026, then total reviews per city and month
city_month_reviews <- reviews_with_city |>
  dplyr::filter(month >= "2025-07", month <= "2026-06") |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, month) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_reviews = sum(reviews, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

city_month_reviews

# Step 4: Focus on Twin Cities, sort to find busiest and quietest months
twin_cities_months <- city_month_reviews |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total_reviews))

twin_cities_months

# A8: busiest month (top row)
a8_busiest <- twin_cities_months |>
  dplyr::slice(1)

a8_busiest
# August 2025 (2025-08)

# A9: ratio of busiest to quietest
busiest_count  <- max(twin_cities_months$total_reviews)
quietest_count <- min(twin_cities_months$total_reviews)
a9_ratio <- busiest_count / quietest_count

a9_ratio
# 2.372235


```


## Task 7
```{r}

entire_homes_known_host <- listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    host_is_superhost %in% c("t", "f")
  )


city_host_summary <- entire_homes_known_host |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, host_is_superhost) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price  = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rating = median(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

city_host_summary


premium_by_city <- city_host_summary |>
  dplyr::select(city, host_is_superhost, median_price) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = host_is_superhost,
    values_from = median_price,
    names_prefix = "median_price_"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(premium = median_price_t - median_price_f)

premium_by_city

# B1: the three premiums, one per city
b1_result <- premium_by_city |>
  dplyr::select(city, premium)

b1_result
# Chicago 43.8, Cbus 40.5, TwinCities -1.38
```
